episodes.155318: A passing inside slider brought gusty winds in the mountains and deserts, along with patchy fog near the coast. The system on February 12 was strong enough and further west and produce a narrow area of heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms along the San Bernardino and Riverside County mountains foothills.
episodes.156584: A complex low pressure system brought with it deep moisture from the Gulf of Mexico as it moved across the central Appalachians.  While much of the precipitation fell in frozen form, warm ground conditions caused some of it to melt upon contact with the surface, resulting in saturated soil conditions.  In addition, daytime temperatures rising above freezing may have resulted in repeated freeze-thaw events that loosened soil and rock, making for conditions that were favorable for debris flows.

events.narrative: A debris flow was reported on Ingleside Road near the intersection with Ada Dam Road,  blocking both lanes of traffic until the debris was cleared.  No damage was reported.

Narrow band of thunderstorms formed along the foothills of the San Bernardino mountains during the morning of February 12th. This heavy rain reached 0.30 inches in 30 minutes and caused minor mud and debris flow from El Dorado burn scar in Yucaipa and Oak Glen.
